scenes.headline: One cyberattack. Factories and shipping stalled.
scenes.body: What it cost, and what every business can learn
scenes.say: Boston Scientific's factories and shipping stalled after one cyberattack. Here is what it cost, and what every business can learn from it.

scenes.headline: A global maker of heart and medical devices
scenes.body: Pacemakers, cardiac ablation systems · 2025 revenue: $20.1 billion
scenes.say: Boston Scientific makes medical devices such as pacemakers and cardiac ablation systems. It reported twenty point one billion dollars in revenue last year.

scenes.headline: From outage to the bill
scenes.say: On August twenty-fifth, the company found unauthorized activity on its systems, and a network outage followed. The next day, it disclosed the incident to the US regulator, the SEC. On September eighth, it warned investors it would likely miss its forecasts. And on October twenty-eighth, third-quarter results showed the cost.

scenes.headline: Systems went dark, so orders could not ship
scenes.body: The outage cut access to some operating systems and business applications
scenes.say: The outage cut access to some operating systems and business applications. For a while, the company could not manufacture, process or ship some customer orders.

scenes.headline: business days of disrupted manufacturing and shipping
scenes.body: As reported from the October 28 earnings call
scenes.say: According to reports of the earnings call, manufacturing and shipments were disrupted for eight business days.

scenes.headline: sales growth, below a 3 to 5% outlook
scenes.body: Net sales: $5.138 billion · management: attack cut about 3 points of growth
scenes.say: Third-quarter sales grew just one point five percent, to five point one three eight billion dollars, below an outlook of three to five percent. Management estimated the attack cut about three points of growth.

scenes.headline: Fourth-quarter sales now expected to fall
scenes.body: Q4: down 1% to 3% · Full-year growth about 4.25%, down from 5.5% to 6.5% in July
scenes.say: The damage runs past the quarter. Boston Scientific now expects fourth-quarter sales to fall one to three percent, and full-year growth of about four and a quarter percent, down from five and a half to six and a half percent in July.

scenes.headline: How the attackers got in: not disclosed
scenes.body: No group has publicly claimed it. Ransomware and data theft are not confirmed.
scenes.say: What we still do not know matters too. So far, the company has not disclosed how the attackers got in. No group has publicly claimed the attack, and ransomware or data theft have not been confirmed.

scenes.headline: working with urgency and resilience to restore operations
scenes.say: Chief executive Mike Mahoney praised his teams for working with urgency and resilience to restore operations.

scenes.headline: Downtime is the real price tag.
scenes.body: The break-in is one moment. Lost days of making and shipping show up in the results.
scenes.say: Analyst note: in attacks like this, downtime is the real price tag. The break-in is one moment. The lost days of making and shipping products are what show up in the results.

scenes.headline: Four lessons
items: List what must keep running if IT goes dark
Rehearse a manual way to take and ship orders
Keep offline backups, and test restoring them
Separate factory systems from office IT
scenes.say: Four lessons for any business. List what must keep running if IT goes dark. Rehearse a manual way to take and ship orders. Keep offline backups, and test restoring them. And separate factory systems from office IT.
